chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Abu Hammam Isma'il ibn Hammam, who said:

Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him) said regarding a man who marries a woman and marries his daughter to her son, then divorces her, and another man marries her and she bears a daughter from him; he disliked that one of his sons marry her because she was his wife (mother of the son), so he divorced her, and she became like a mother to him, and before that she was a mother to him. This report came explicitly indicating the dislike (karahah) that we mentioned.

key_terms.بِمَنْزِلَةِ الْأَبِ: In the status/position of a father (referring to the mother's status relative to the son-in-law).
key_terms.فَارَقَهَا: He divorced her (specifically referring to the act of separation/divorce).
key_terms.كَرَاهِيَة: Dislike or preference in Islamic jurisprudence, indicating a recommended but not obligatory action or a discouraged but not forbidden state.

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a man to marry his step-daughter if he divorced her mother?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Istibsar clarifies the distinction between absolute prohibition (mahram) and recommended dislike (karahat) in the case of a man marrying the daughter of his ex-wife from another husband. The Imam establishes that while the marital bond with the mother is severed by divorce, the relational status of 'motherhood' persists, rendering the step-daughter akin to a daughter for the purpose of this recommended dislike, rather than a strict impediment to marriage.
